content.title: About
content.content: Provolone is a semi‑hard Italian cheese made from cow’s milk. The reduced‑fat version has a portion of the butterfat removed, making it lower in calories while retaining its characteristic nutty flavor and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Provolone is traditionally used as a melting cheese for casseroles and sandwiches.
The cheese is named after the town of Provolone in Italy, where it was first produced in the 19th century.
Reduced‑fat provolone appeared in the 1970s in response to growing demand for low‑fat dairy products.
It is often used as a mozzarella substitute on pizza because it melts more smoothly.
The cheese can be aged up to 6 months, developing a richer taste over time.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Reduced‑fat provolone provides about 28 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Fat typically does not exceed 5 g per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: The cheese is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provolone contains riboflavin (B2) and vitamin B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Like most aged cheeses, provolone contains live cultures that can support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although aged cheeses have lower lactose, people with severe intolerance may still experience symptoms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The cheese can contain up to 600 mg of sodium per 100 g, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to casein, the main milk protein.

items.title: Shelf‑life control
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth, rendering the cheese unsafe to eat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑fat provolone works well in casseroles, pizza, pasta, sandwiches, and salads. Slice it thin, grate it, or melt it as a top layer on hot dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. For longer storage (over 2 weeks), wrap it in wax paper followed by aluminum foil to prevent drying. Do not keep at room temperature for more than 4 hours.
